blocks.x: Disney’s relationship with Fortnite has already put some of its biggest characters into the game's bonkers playground. Marvel heroes and Star Wars villains can share a match without anyone needing to explain how their universes collided. Those collaborations helped establish Epic Games as a place where Disney could reach players beyond traditional adaptations of its movies.

The companies made that relationship considerably bigger in February 2024, when Disney announced a $1.5 billion investment in Epic alongside plans for a connected games and entertainment universe. The project promised experiences drawing from properties including Marvel and Star Wars, with opportunities to play and create. It was an ambitious pitch, even for companies already accustomed to working with enormous audiences.

Epic is now reportedly directing staff to use an “AI-first” development process on an unannounced Disney shooter featuring Marvel and Star Wars characters. According to new reports, an internal message instructed developers to use “no more handwritten code” and said the game’s art would be produced through AI workflows. The report describes humans guiding that work, with tools including Anthropic’s Claude involved in production.

Which Sci-Fi Hero Are You Most Like?
Paul Atreides · Captain Kirk · Princess Leia · Ellen Ripley · Max Rockatansky

Five iconic heroes. Five completely different ways of facing an impossible universe. One of them shares your instincts, your values, and your particular way of refusing to back down. Eight questions will tell you which one.
🏜️Paul Atreides
🖖Capt. Kirk
✊Princess Leia
🔦Ellen Ripley
🔥Max Rockatansky
FIND YOUR HERO →

How do you lead when the stakes couldn't be higher?
The way you lead under pressure is the most honest thing about you.

AI absorb everything — every variable, every pattern — and move only when I know the path forward.
BI read the room, make the call, and own the consequences. Hesitation costs more than mistakes.
CI rally people. A cause needs a voice, and I refuse to let fear be louder than conviction.
DI assess the threat, establish what needs doing, and get it done without waiting for permission.
EI don't lead. I act. Others can follow or not — I'm already moving.
NEXT QUESTION →

What is your greatest strength in a crisis?
The quality that keeps you alive when everything else fails.

APrescience — the ability to see further ahead than anyone else and plan accordingly.
BImprovisation — I'm at my best when the plan falls apart and I have to invent a new one.
CConviction — I know what I'm fighting for, and that certainty doesn't waver under fire.
DComposure — I stay functional when everyone around me is falling apart. Panic is a luxury.
EEndurance — I outlast things. I take the hit and keep moving long after others have stopped.
NEXT QUESTION →

What is the thing you'd sacrifice everything else for?
Your deepest motivation is your truest compass.

AThe survival and dignity of my people — even if I have to become something frightening to ensure it.
BThe safety of my crew — every single one of them. No one gets left behind.
CFreedom — for my people, for every world still crushed under the weight of an empire.
DThe truth — what actually happened, what's actually out there, whether anyone believes me or not.
EThe one person — or the one memory — that still makes any of this worth surviving for.
NEXT QUESTION →

How do you relate to the people around you?
Who you are to others under pressure is who you really are.

AWith intensity and distance — I care deeply, but the weight I carry makes closeness complicated.
BWith warmth and irreverence — I take the mission seriously, not myself.
CWith directness and trust — I say what I mean, and I expect the people I work with to rise to it.
DWith professional care but clear limits — I'll protect you, but I won't pretend we're family.
EWith wariness that slowly becomes loyalty — I don't trust easily, but when I do, it holds.
NEXT QUESTION →

You're facing a threat that no one else believes is real. What do you do?
How you respond when you're the only one who sees it defines everything.

APrepare in silence. If they won't listen, I'll be ready when they finally have to.
BKeep pushing until someone listens — and if no one does, handle it myself.
CBuild the case, find the allies, and make the threat impossible to ignore.
DDocument everything. The truth matters even if no one believes it yet.
EStop trying to convince anyone. Survive it. That's the only argument that counts.
NEXT QUESTION →

What has your heroism cost you personally?
Every hero pays. The question is what — and whether they'd pay it again.

AMy innocence — I've seen what I'm capable of, and I can't unsee it.
BPeople I loved — the command chair has a view, but it's a lonely one.
CA normal life — I gave up everything ordinary the moment I chose the cause.
DMy sense of safety — I know exactly what's out there now, and I can't pretend otherwise.
EAlmost everything — and I'm still not sure what I'm carrying it all for. But I keep going.
NEXT QUESTION →

How do you feel about the rules of the world you're in?
Every hero has a relationship with the system. What's yours?

AI understand them deeply — and I know exactly which ones must be broken, and why.
BI respect the spirit of them and bend the letter when the situation demands it.
CThe system is the problem. I'm not here to work within it — I'm here to dismantle it.
DI follow protocol until protocol stops being useful. Then I make the call myself.
EThe rules collapsed a long time ago. What's left is instinct, and mine are reliable.
NEXT QUESTION →

When everything is on the line, what keeps you going?
The answer is the most honest thing about you.

ADestiny — or something that feels so much like it that the difference no longer matters.
BThe people on my ship — their faces, their trust, the fact that they're counting on me.
CThe belief that what we're fighting for is worth every sacrifice, including this one.
DSheer refusal to let it win — whatever it is. I don't stop. That's just who I am.
EI'm not sure anymore. But the road is still there, and I'm still on it.

You have been through fire that would break most people — and what came out the other side is something the world underestimates at its peril.
You don't ask for help, don't need validation, and don't wait for anyone to tell you the rules no longer apply.
Your loyalty, when it finally arrives, is absolute — but it's earned in silence and tested in action, not in words.
Max is not a nihilist. He is someone who lost everything and found, against his will, that he still has something worth protecting.
That bruised, stubborn, ultimately human core is exactly yours.

The reported instructions go considerably further than using AI for an occasional task. They would make generated material central to both the game’s code and its art, with developers responsible for directing and managing the results. Bloomberg reports that some staff members were stunned by the announcement, which followed slower-than-expected progress and an underestimate of the staffing required. That puts the proposed production change alongside an existing development problem. Epic’s public response emphasizes the people overseeing the technology.

A spokesperson told the publication that the company is embracing AI-accelerated development while describing Epic’s developers as its creative drivers. CEO Tim Sweeney also acknowledged a broader push toward AI, saying staff was being moved around to support it. He framed the goal as increasing what employees could build, rather than doing the same work with fewer people. The frustrating part is that Epic reportedly underestimated how many developers the project needed, and its answer is to put AI at the center of production. The people hired to make the game would instead be expected to guide the generated work and fix whatever comes back wrong. Generating something faster doesn’t make it worth using, and checking that output still takes time and expertise.

Calling the process “AI-first” does nothing to explain why it would produce a better game than giving developers the resources they needed in the first place. That’s an especially disappointing direction for a project built around Marvel and Star Wars, franchises whose appeal owes so much to the artists who created them. Fans want to see what talented developers can do with those worlds, and a collaboration of this scale should give them room to do it.

The shooter still has no announced title or release date, leaving players without footage to judge against Epic’s promises. Until there’s something to show, the company’s enthusiasm for AI is a lot more visible than the game itself. Stay tuned at Collider for more updates.
